messages:
shweta: Heads up— multiple users hit import issues after following Quickstart. Examples are inconsistent: some show `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'`, others `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'`.

owen: Yep. Support is getting `TypeError: Redwood is not a constructor` and `Cannot use import statement outside a module` reports. Most are just trying to copy paste.

diego: Quick triage: our package CJS entry exports named symbols only. `require('@redwood/inference')` yields an object with `RedwoodClient` but no `default`. TS projects with `esModuleInterop` often mask the issue which makes it confusing.

shweta: Proposal: immediate docs patch to standardize on named imports in examples and add a short FAQ entry about `require` vs `import`, `esModuleInterop`, and edge runtimes.

owen: Agreed. Add explicit snippets for both Node CJS and ESM and a one-liner for Edge runtimes like Vercel/CF: "use the ESM build or ensure bundler preserves named exports".

diego: Longer term we should publish compatibility shims in the CJS build (`module.exports.default = exports.RedwoodClient`) and add `export default RedwoodClient` in the ESM types/build to satisfy both patterns.

shweta: I'll open the docs PR and a follow-up packaging PR. Draft doc snippet I'll include:

```
// ESM (recommended)
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })

// CommonJS
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference')
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })
```

owen: Nice. Also add note: "If you wrote `import Redwood from` and it worked, you probably have `esModuleInterop` enabled; prefer named import for portability."

docs-bot: New docs PR created by shweta: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/219 (title: "standardize JS Quickstart imports + FAQ")

shweta: Thanks all. Targeting merge today and patch release afterwards. I'll add migration notes to changelog.
